g.text: Ad attribution — the store, and what it must be able to un-say
1 right first time · 2 corrected · 2 never delivered
2 // Two of a row's five columns are CLOCKS, which ch01 established:
3 // et = event time, when it happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // key = which stream it is on: "a" = clicks, "b" = impressions
5 type Row { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 rows, in ARRIVAL order (tools/stream_seed.js).
7 // EVENTS[7] = (id 7, key "b", et 50, pt 280, v 4) <- the late impression
8 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
9 // primitive: J — the join window, in seconds. J = 60
10 // primitive: LAG — each side's assumed worst-case skew. LAG = 60
11 // primitive: KEYS — the two sides. KEYS = ["a", "b"]
12 // primitive: LEFT / RIGHT — the side names. LEFT = "a" · RIGHT = "b"
13 // primitive: rowsOf(key) — one side of the join.
15 // primitive: absDiff(a, b) — the distance between two times. absDiff(1, 50) = 49
16 // primitive: append(xs, x) — xs with x added at the end. append([1], 2) = [1,2]
17 // primitive: indexOf(r) — r's position in ARRIVAL order. indexOf(EVENTS[7]) = 7
22 // primitive: rowById(id) — the row with that id.
24 // primitive: emitFor(l) — what the join publishes for a click: MATCH, NO-MATCH,
29 // primitive: matchesOf(clickId) — that click's true impressions.
31 // primitive: contradictedBy(l) — impressions arriving after the emission.
34 // function: attribute(store, clickId, impressions) — write an attribution row.
41 // function: markUnattributed(store, clickId) — publish a NEGATIVE result. This is
42 // the row that later has to be withdrawn.
49 // function: retract(store, clickId, canTombstone) — un-say a published claim. For a
50 // NEGATIVE claim, overwriting is not enough: a consumer that already read
51 // "NONE MATCHED" needs to be told it was withdrawn.
53 // retract(store, 0, false).tombstones = [] (the consumer is never told)
60 // function: run(canTombstone) — the whole attribution pipeline over this stream.
61 // run(true).rows has 3 attributed clicks and 2 tombstone
62 // run(false) leaves the same rows and no record that 2 claim was withdrawn
79 // function: main() — THE CALLER: with and without tombstones.
Step 1/0 — the join publishes a NEGATIVE attribution
`rows[0] = "NONE MATCHED"` — a published claim that this click was never attributed. At the moment it is written it is the correct answer from everything
that has arrived, which is what makes it dangerous: it is indistinguishable from a settled fact.

Step 2/0 — then a late impression contradicts it
`late` holds impression 7, which arrived at row 7 — 2 rows after the emission — and is 49s from the click. The branch fires, so the published "NONE MATCHED"
has to be withdrawn and replaced.

Step 3/0 — retracting a negative needs a TOMBSTONE, not an overwrite
The tombstone is the record that a claim was withdrawn. Overwriting `rows[0]` fixes the store, but a consumer that already read "NONE MATCHED" and acted on
it never learns otherwise — which is why an updating sink is not sufficient here and an explicit retraction is.

Step 4/0 — and without it the two stores look identical
Both stores end with the same 3 attributed clicks; only `tombstones` differs. So the damage from omitting retractions is invisible in the store's final state
— and note neither store mentions the 2 click that never emitted at all, holding 2 of the 5 true matches.
